pairs.difference: A: low camera, valve near the top of the ball, sand runs back to a soft dune band, so ground and backdrop read as two layers. B: camera looks down from high, valve near the ball's centre, sand fills the whole card with no horizon (lens is one green-teal field), and the ball fills most of the frame.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera to just above the sand. Show the valve near the top of the ball, make the ball smaller, and add a simple backdrop behind a clear line where the sand ends.

pairs.difference: A: wooden frame seen almost flat-on, with thin inner sides on the posts, and a level shelf. B: both frame posts show wide inner side faces (large pink and green strips in the lens), a tunnel-like wide-angle view. The target and bear are turned to their own angles inside it. The difference is modest, because A's target also turns away from its easel.
pairs.fix: Flatten the frame to a mild view: the posts show only a thin inner edge, and the target, easel and bear turn by the same small angle.

pairs.difference: Both show a wall unit seen from below and to the left, with the top and bottom edges converging mildly and the side cap in pink on the right. A has a room corner and ceiling; B has a ceiling moulding. Each moulding or ceiling line agrees with its unit's angle. Both planar_share values sit above the listed range, so they do not separate the cards.

A: chest turned clearly to three-quarter, side face wide, on a soft plain sand hump against a simple blue backdrop. B: more front-on chest with a narrower side face, seen from slightly higher, with the sand plane rising further up the card and carrying more detail, close to the generated habit in the lessons.
pairs.fix: Turn the chest further so its side face is nearly as wide as half the front. Lower the camera a little and keep the sand a low, plain band.

pairs.difference: A: low camera, the wall meets the floor in one near-level line, floorboards recede gently, and the cap sits firmly on that floor. B: the floor is seen from high, with steep diagonal boards and a room corner with skirting boards running in two directions (strong pink and blue wall patches), while the cap's visor and band are seen from a much lower eye level, so the cap does not sit in the same view as the floor.
pairs.fix: Use one low camera for cap and floor: a plain flat wall behind, a near-level line where wall meets floor, shallow floorboards, and no room corner.

pairs.difference: A: the booth narrows toward its base, seen from above, with a domed roof that swells in the lens, a stronger forced convergence than real cards. B: the booth's vertical edges stay nearly parallel, and the roof and base agree on one mild view, like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Keep the booth's vertical edges almost parallel, with no narrowing toward the base, and show only a thin slice of the roof top.

pairs.difference: A: camera above the floor, the gloves lie on receding boards with cuffs pointing back, and both gloves are the same size at one angle. B: very low close camera, the front glove looms and pushes to the card edges, the floor is a thin band, the rear glove is turned to a different view, and the lens shows large balloon-like rainbows.
pairs.fix: Raise the camera and move it back. Lay both gloves side by side on the floor at the same angle and about the same size, with floorboards receding behind them.

pairs.difference: A: both fins foreshorten steadily at one diagonal angle, with thin blades tapering to crisp ends. B: same diagonal, but the blades swell wide toward the viewer, with a thick rounded rim along the near end in the lens, a mild wide-angle bulge.
pairs.fix: Keep the blades thin and flat, with no thick near rim, and make the near ends no wider than the rest, so both fins recede evenly.

pairs.difference: A: low camera, level horizon, the pier recedes in mild perspective with sand foreground, pier, then sea and sky as clear layers. B: steep close-up from above with no horizon, the near post and lifebuoy loom huge, the planks rush away diagonally, and the water fills the card as one flat field, a forced wide-angle view.
pairs.fix: Pull the camera back and lower it to a level sea horizon. Show the whole small pier receding gently, with sand in front and sky behind, and all posts close in size.

pairs.difference: A: crown and trunk share one side view, with fronds arching over coconuts and a cast shadow lying on the sand. B: the crown splays flat like a star seen from nearly in front of its centre, with coconuts hidden beneath it, while the trunk and rocks are seen from the side, so the crown and trunk read as two views.
pairs.fix: Draw the crown from the same side view as the trunk: fronds arch up and droop down, and coconuts sit visibly under them. Lay a cast shadow on the sand.

pairs.difference: A: the skirting board and floor slope in step with the locker's bottom edge, so locker and room share one turned view from above. B: the wall and skirting are dead level and frontal, but the locker's top and bottom front edges slope apart strongly, so it is turned to a different angle from the room it stands in.
pairs.fix: Turn the wall, skirting board and floorboards to the same angle as the locker, so its bottom edge runs parallel to the skirting board.

pairs.difference: A: the whole slide is seen from a moderate distance, with the deck curving into the pool and the structure fitting one mild view. B: low close camera, the upper tube sweeps across the frame and the mouth lunges at the viewer, with sizes changing sharply along the slide and the deck squeezed to a thin strip.
pairs.fix: Move the camera back and slightly higher so the whole spiral fits, the slide's width stays nearly even from top to bottom, and the deck shows as a wide plane.

pairs.difference: A: the player is a compact block seen from a clear three-quarter angle, with a straight side wall on the lower right, and the earbuds lie around it at one scale. B: a soft pillow with no distinct side wall, a broad front patch that rounds away at the edges, and earbuds growing large toward the viewer at the bottom.
pairs.fix: Draw a firm block with a flat front and one straight side wall visible, and keep the earbuds at the same scale and distance as the player.

pairs.difference: A: a flat paper envelope rotated in the plane of the card, with almost no thickness, like the real flat ticket; its planar_share of 0.855 is above the real range, which argues against this call. B: an upright envelope with a thick rounded lower lip and sides visible, inflated like a cushion with depth paper would not have.
pairs.fix: Make the envelope thin paper with no thick rounded edge, tilt it slightly, and let the depth come only from the overlapping photos.

pairs.difference: A: low camera, plate a shallow ellipse, with a table edge and striped wall behind giving two ground layers. B: camera high over the table, plate a wide open ellipse, diagonal boards fill the card with no backdrop (one blue lens field), and the fruit lies pressed against the plate.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera to just above the table so the plate is a thin ellipse, with fruit standing up from it, and add a plain wall behind a level table edge.

pairs.difference: Both doors are seen head-on, with inner reveals on both sides of the frame, one consistent view. A crops close with no ground; B shows the whole arch with a paving step. That is framing more than camera. A's planar_share of 0.012 looks like a lens failure on its busy foliage, since the door panels themselves read flat.

pattern: Generated cards tend to use a more extreme or less unified camera than real cards. The camera sits high with ground filling the card and no horizon (ball, fruit plate, dock), or very close with the nearest part looming (dock, gloves, slide). Parts also disagree on view: a fan-flat palm crown on a side-view trunk, a turned locker in a frontal room, a cap at a lower eye level than its floor. Forms swell into cushions without a distinct flat side wall (music player, envelope, gloves). Real cards stay mild, keep hero and ground at one angle, and separate ground and backdrop simply.
